name: BulkCertPDF
summary: Turns an Excel or CSV attendee list into named PDF certificates, with 8 designs, your logo and signatures.
best_for: training providers, course organisers and HR teams who need named PDF certificates from a spreadsheet without designing each one
skip_if: you need certificates linked to a learning platform, you want to keep attendee data off third-party tools, or you want a tool we have tested ourselves
honest_knock: The free plan stops at 25 certificates a month and prints a small 'Made with BulkCertPDF' line on each, and the Batch Pass expires after 7 days. We did not check how the hosted verification pages handle personal data.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-18 on bulkcertpdf.com/pricing, US dollars; earlier: read 2026-11-11) BulkCertPDF has a Free plan, a one-off Batch Pass and a Pro subscription. Free costs $0, takes an Excel or CSV upload, includes all 8 designs, your logo and signatures, and covers 25 certificates a month. Free certificates carry a small 'Made with BulkCertPDF' line, which the page says is not a watermark; lists bigger than your remaining allowance show a watermarked preview until you buy a pass. The Batch Pass costs $19 once and covers up to 500 certificates without a watermark; it gives 7 days of access and is not a subscription. Pro costs $29 a month or $199 a year, shown as $16.58 a month and a 43% saving, and allows unlimited certificates and batches without a watermark; the page says you can cancel any time. The page shows a 14-day money-back guarantee and secure checkout by Lemon Squeezy, and says taxes are calculated at checkout where they apply.

schema_offer.description: Pro monthly, Pro is $29 a month or $199 a year (shown as $16.58 a month); Batch Pass is $19 once for up to 500 certificates and 7 days of access; Free is $0 for 25 certificates a month. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-18.

free_plan_evidence: (read 2026-11-18 on bulkcertpdf.com/pricing, US dollars; earlier: read 2026-11-11) BulkCertPDF has a Free plan, a one-off Batch Pass and a Pro subscription.

compare_with.name: Certifier
compare_with.why: Certifier is a certificate platform with an account and automation, while BulkCertPDF turns one spreadsheet into one ZIP. Run the same 25-name list through each free plan and compare the time and the look of the result

claims.claim: Small "Made with BulkCertPDF" line, no watermark
claims.observed: The pricing page says the Free plan has a small Made with BulkCertPDF line and no watermark, and the preview shows a small line at the bottom of the certificate. The dossier says Free has a watermark, which contradicts the page wording; the ZIP itself was not opened.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the pricing section was read without clicking a buy button
claims.comparability: The dossier wording against the pricing page and the preview; the files in the ZIP were not opened, so the line in the PDFs was not seen.
claims.buying_consequence: Free certificates carry a small branding line, not a watermark across the page, so the dossier word is too strong for what the page and the preview show.

claims.observed: After one batch of 5 recipients the Free counter went from 25 to 20 left this month, which fits a limit of 25 per month; the month reset and the sixth to the twenty-fifth certificate were not tried.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the pricing section was read without clicking a buy button
claims.comparability: The pricing page limit against the counter before and after one batch; only the drop by 5 was observed.
claims.buying_consequence: Five certificates cost five of the free monthly quota, so a batch larger than what is left needs a paid plan.

claims.claim: ZIP, print PDF or single files
claims.observed: The Free plan generated a ZIP batch of 5 recipients, but the ZIP was not opened and the print PDF and single file options were not used, so the output is not checked.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the pricing section was read without clicking a buy button
claims.comparability: The pricing page wording against a batch that was generated but not opened; the preview and the counter only.
claims.buying_consequence: What the generated certificates look like in the files, including the raw tags, is not shown by this test.

claims.claim: Your spreadsheet never leaves your browser
claims.observed: The page says the spreadsheet is processed locally; no network traffic was inspected, so this was neither confirmed nor contradicted.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the pricing section was read without clicking a buy button
claims.comparability: A privacy statement on the page against a test that only used made-up names and did not look at network requests.
claims.buying_consequence: Privacy of the recipient names cannot be judged from this test.

claims.observed: The pricing section shows the Batch Pass at $19 one-off with up to 500 certificates and 7 days of access; the button was not clicked, so no tax, total or payment screen was seen.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the pricing section was read without clicking a buy button

exit_test.what: No account was needed; the tool ran without signing in. On 18 November 2026 the session tested BulkCertPDF without an account on the Free plan: a CSV with 5 made-up names became a batch of certificates in about 6 seconds and the Free counter went from 25 to 20 left. A name of 86 characters runs to the edge of the paper and is not made smaller, and columns the CSV does not have stay on the certificate as raw tags such as CPD_Hours and Certificate_Ref without any warning. The pricing page calls the Free branding a small line with no watermark, while the dossier says watermark. The ZIP file itself was not opened, so its contents are not tested. No plan was bought. Account and start: no account was needed. The tool works without a login ("Free for 25 certificates a month, no signup") and shows a counter in the header. The test started at 09:06 in our own tab on the tool page, with the counter at 25 of 25 left this month. There is no language setting; the interface was already English. The dossier name is BulkCertPDF and the review is on OSM (bulkcertpdf-review); the handson folder name and the review slug are the same. Core action: a CSV file with 5 made-up recipients (columns Full Name, Course Title and Completion Date) was uploaded and the tool showed 5 recipients. Four names were short test names and the fifth was a made-up name of 86 characters. The design Official CPD was already selected. After looking at the preview, one click on Generate All 5 PDFs (.ZIP) Free produced the batch in about 6 seconds (not timed precisely) and the counter went from 25 to 20 of 25 left this month. In all this took 2 actions: the upload and the generate click. The tool sends nothing by email to the recipients. What the preview showed: the 86-character name did not fit; it runs to the edge of the paper and touches the inner border at both sides, and it is not made smaller. The certificate text contained the merge tags CPD_Hours and Certificate_Ref because our CSV had no such columns; the tags stay on the certificate as raw text and the tool gives no warning. The bottom of the certificate has a small line Made with BulkCertPDF. At the end a box asks for an email address for templates and a monthly newsletter; it was not filled in. The sample signature on the certificate was covered by the tester. The ZIP file itself was NOT opened. Only the preview and the counter were seen, so what the generated PDFs contain (the name, the raw tags, the branding line, the page layout) is not tested. Plans, read up to the payment step on the pricing section: Free $0 (Upload Excel or CSV, All 8 designs, logo and signatures, 25 certificates a month as ZIP, print PDF or single files, and the line Small Made with BulkCertPDF line, no watermark), Batch Pass $19 one-off (up to 500 certificates, no watermark or branding, ZIP of PDFs and a merged print PDF, 7 days of access, no subscription) and Pro $29 a month or $199 a year (unlimited certificates and batches, no watermark or branding, cancel anytime). The page also says 14-day money-back guarantee, secure checkout by Lemon Squeezy and that the spreadsheet never leaves your browser. Taxes (UK VAT, Australian GST, US sales tax) are calculated at checkout. A Saved design option is marked Pro. Nothing was clicked on the plans. Deviation from the dossier: the dossier says the Free plan has a watermark. The pricing page says literally Small Made with BulkCertPDF line, no watermark, and the preview shows a small branding line at the bottom, not a watermark across the certificate. The dossier and the page contradict each other on this word. The prices and the limits match the dossier. No price field is changed here. Checkout: NOT reached. No plan was bought, no buy button was clicked, and no tax, total, card or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: there is no account and no subscription, so there was nothing to cancel. Not tested: the contents of the ZIP, Batch Pass and Pro, hosted verification pages and what happens with personal data there, a logo upload, an Excel upload, US Letter, and cancelling. Clean up: nothing to delete; there is no account. The Free counter lost 5 of 25 certificates (it now says 20 left). The browser may keep a local recent list. The test file with the made-up names stays outside the evidence. The tab was closed.
exit_test.awkward: A very long name is not made smaller and runs to the edge of the paper. Merge tags without a matching CSV column stay on the certificate as raw text such as CPD_Hours, and the tool does not warn you. Saved designs are a Pro feature. The Free certificates carry a small Made with BulkCertPDF line.
